*Brightline Train Development CEO: Agreement to Help Balance Sheet Match Growth Already Seen Across Business
*WSJ Had Previously Reported That Brightline Was Planning Bankruptcy Filing to Restructure About $5.5B Debt
Brightline Florida Gets $490M in New Financing Under Restructuring Deal
By Megan Cheah and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa
Florida high-speed rail system Brightline has announced a restructuring deal to cut down debt and secure $490 million of new capital.

The restructuring agreement was reached between certain entities associated with the company and financial stakeholders--including Assured Guaranty--and a group of mutual fund bondholders, Brightline said Friday.
The $490 million of financing consists of $140 million in additional senior debt and $350 million of new junior debt.
"This transaction will be a catalyst for further growth in ridership and revenue," said Patrick Goddard, chief executive of Brightline Florida.
Certain Brightline parent entities will start bankruptcy proceedings in New Jersey to implement the agreement.

Brightline Trains Florida LLC won't file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and will continue operating under existing management. Brightline Florida Holdings LLC, which indirectly holds the rights to develop commuter services in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach Counties, is also not part of the process, nor is AAF Operations Holdings LLC, which indirectly holds Tampa development rights.

Several bond issues, including $2.2 billion of Brightline Trains Florida LLC Series 2024 bonds, and the existing bond insurance policy issued by Assured Guaranty, will remain in place through the restructuring.

Separately, Assured Guaranty, whose subsidiary insures slightly over 50% of Brightline Trains Florida LLC's existing senior bonds, said its subsidiary and some financial stakeholders will provide the company $258 million of post-petition funding while those Brightline entities undergo the bankruptcy process.
The funding--which will be considered "pari passu", or on equal treatment, with the existing senior debt--will be repaid upon those entities' exit from the bankruptcy process.

Specific bondholders have also agreed to a limited deferral of scheduled interest payments on certain senior bonds, in exchange for a fee paid by Brightline Trains Florida LLC, Assured Guaranty said. Brightline Trains Florida LLC will offer this option to all senior bondholders, Assured Guaranty added.

Nicolas Petrovic, chief executive of affiliate Brightline Train Development LLC, said the restructuring won't affect operations. "It will give Brightline the balance sheet to match the growth we're already seeing across the business."

The Wall Street Journal had previously reported that the Fortress Investment Group-backed company was planning an imminent chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in New Jersey to restructure about $5.5 billion in debt.
The company had been negotiating with creditors for more than a year to restructure its debt out of court, the Journal reported Wednesday.
Brightline amassed a total of $5.5 billion in debt through a combination of municipal bonds, taxable debt and so-called commuter bonds to help fund its plan to connect major cities across Florida.

However, ridership failed to grow fast enough to sustain its heavy debt burden. The company issued a going-concern warning in April that spurred senior municipal bondholders, bond insurers and junior debtholders to offer competing financing.
